The methods in this family share the mechanism of hierarchical decomposition and error-driven or distance-driven primitive selection, building on [Splatting](23-splatting.md).
**Adaptive Traversal and Selection:** During rendering, the hierarchy is traversed from the root to the leaves.
**Primitive Aggregation:** When a node is selected, its children are merged into a single representative primitive.
To determine splat depth relation, pair up multi-layer surface intersections at splat center $p$ with closest intersections at target pixel $q$ in depth.
- **Pitfall:** Single-layer splatting treats all splats at the same depth, ignoring occlusions and producing spurious derivatives for occluded objects.
The concept of hierarchical splatting emerged alongside the need for real-time volume rendering.
Early implementations focused on accelerating the evaluation of splats using spatial data structures.
In the context of Gaussian Splatting, hierarchical methods have been adapted to handle dynamic deformations and multi-resolution rendering.
